# T1a ceiling kill test (+ conditional T1b): structural pins and the
# per-plane group repair

- **Role:** the Builder
- **Date:** 2026-08-26 (Builder slice Q1 of the T-series program, PR #146,
  issue #130)
- **Authority:** spec addendum 20 (algorithmic-spec.md section 20) and the
  T-series blueprint (`architecture-jxl-parity-tseries.md` sections 2/7)

## P-Q1-1 REPAIR FIRST: group identity becomes per-plane (amendment-grade, pre-measurement)

Addendum 20.2 GROUP GEOMETRY is explicit: "group id = raster order within
the plane; group identity is per-plane (no cross-plane grouping)", and the
first Q0 pin record (2026-08-26T08-00-00) repeated it ("planes never share
a stack"). The shipped `ClusterMap::raw_at` KGROUP path computes g from
(x, y) only, so all three planes pool into the SAME tile stacks - a
counting-layout violation of the pinned design that no committed unit test
contradicts (the geometry tests are single-plane). P-T0-13's own guard
arithmetic (288 groups x 16 classes = 4608 joint rows for GS64 on a
768x512 plane set) only makes sense per-plane; the pooled implementation
allocates a third of that.

Repair, landed before any quad number exists:

    ClusterMap gains uint32_t group_base = 0   (units: GROUPS)
    KGROUP raw id := (group_base + tile_raster_id) * 16 + class16
    count_joint builds ONE ClusterMap PER PLANE with
        group_base = plane_index * tiles_per_plane
    model clusters = nplanes * tiles_per_plane * 16

Consequences handled in the same commit: every group-keyed counting,
recount, coding and decode site takes its OWN plane's map; a regression
test binds "two planes, same tile position, disjoint content land in
disjoint stacks" plus the exact joint-row count; --t0-synth fixtures follow
the same per-plane maps.

Evidence hygiene (A2/A4b precedent): the Q0 smoke's CEIL/CB rows were
measured under the plane-POOLED variant, so they are voided as evidence
about the pinned design; the committed t0 CSV is REGENERATED with the
repaired instrument in this slice (anchors and T-BASE rows are unaffected
by the repair and stay bit-for-bit). No T-phase verdict ever depended on a
smoke row (P-T0-11), so nothing re-grades.

## P-Q1-2 T1a candidate scope

CEILING candidates sweep {KGROUP64, KGROUP128} x ALL SEVEN D4c color
trials, exactly the trial freedom the T-BASE control already has
(addendum 20.1). Per image the CEILING arm winner is chosen strictly by
real NET bytes among B-RANS rows (payload + tables NETTED; maps = trees =
assign = 0 by construction); ties resolve to the SMALLER tile edge. The
T-BASE control is re-run FRESH in-process per image per addendum 20.1
(ADAPT / SPINE x trials by real NET bytes, ties to ADAPT). B-IDEAL rows
are fidelity-rail diagnostics only and never enter any winner choice.

## P-Q1-3 Gate reading (mechanical)

Per image i, with net_base(i) = the fresh T-BASE winner NET and
net_ceil(i) = the winning CEILING arm's NET:

    relpct(i)     = 100 * (net_base(i) - net_ceil(i)) / net_base(i)
    payload_pct_gain(i) = 100 * (payload_base(i) - payload_ceil(i)) /
                          payload_base(i)

T1a PASS iff median over the quad of relpct(i) >= +2.00 (I10 medians
primary). Every derived figure cites same-run rows only.

## P-Q1-4 Fail clause arithmetic (sole losing term, mechanically readable)

Component deltas are candidate-minus-base-winner per component:
dPayload, dTables, dMaps, dTrees, dAssign (dNET = their sum, asserted).
An image satisfies sole_tables_loss iff

    dTables > 0 AND dPayload <= 0 AND dMaps == 0 AND
    dTrees == 0 AND dAssign == 0

The conditional T1b opener fires iff ALL of:

    median(relpct) < +2.00                       (T1a FAIL)
    median(payload_pct_gain) >= +4.00            (real payload headroom)
    sole_tables_loss true on ALL FOUR images     (tables the SOLE loser,
                                                 conservative whole-set
                                                 reading of addendum 20.5)

## P-Q1-5 Coding tables == transmitted artifact verbatim

Every family codes against EXACTLY the table artifact its decoder can
reconstruct: ceiling rows code under the transmitted 'SBM1' tables;
codebook rows (conditional T1b) code under the TRANSMITTED 'SBC1'
prototype tables indexed by (word(g) * 16 + c). Data-derived rebuilds of
tables from recounted events (the t0 smoke's diagnostic ideal-bits
reference flow) NEVER produce coding tables in Q1; when Lloyd's drop
reassigns groups, recount-smoothed tables diverge from transmitted
prototypes and coding must not use them. Ideal-bit references in T1b are
computed against the transmitted prototypes for the same reason.

## P-Q1-6 Conditional T1b scope and gates

Configurations = {CB4, CB8, CB16, CB24} x {GS64, GS128} (K set measured
WHOLE per addendum 20.2; K > G clamps per pin P-T0-3). Per configuration
per image: sweep all seven color trials, keep the best real-NET B-RANS
row (ties smaller tile edge for GS, lowest K for CB ties). Configuration
statistic = quad median of relpct vs the SAME-RUN T-BASE winners. Winner =
best configuration median, reported ONCE with the whole set printed beside
(no post-hoc re-selection, ever). Gates, BOTH on the winner median:

    retain:  winner_median_relpct >= PG / 2
    floor:   winner_median_relpct >= +1.00

where PG = max(median(payload_pct_gain) over the two T1a arms) from the
same run. Assignment words ride inside 'SBC1' (words tail) and are NETTED
in the assign column; prototype-table bytes are the tables column minus
nothing (serializer decomposition via words_tail).

## P-Q1-7 Rails before verdicts

All six VB rails green on the new families BEFORE any verdict line:
anchors bit-for-bit against the committed reference; VB-proto-roundtrip /
VB-assign-mirror / VB-net-audit-t extended to the T1 row schemas (CEIL
rows carry zero maps/trees/assign; CB rows carry zero maps/trees and a
nonzero words tail; ADAPT carries zero side info); decode round-trip
equality on EVERY coded row; coder fidelity within +0.50 pct per
(img, cand, trial, gs) family; determinism byte-identical full re-run;
quad sha-pins verified pre-run. A gate rejection never flips the exit
code; rail failures always do.

## P-Q1-8 CSV schema

`benchmarks/results/2026-08-26-sandbox-t1a.csv` (+ `-t1b` iff opened), one
file per phase. Row forms:

    T1,<img>,<cand>,<trial>,<gs>,<be>,payload,tables,maps,trees,assign,
        net,audit,rt,tbl_bits,keff,payload_pct_gain
    TSUM,<img>,<arm>,base_payload,base_tables,base_maps,base_trees,
        base_assign,base_net,payload,tables,maps,trees,assign,net,
        payload_pct_gain,relpct,sole_tables_loss

cand in {ADAPT, SPINE, CEIL}; arm in {CEIL@GS64, CEIL@GS128} (T1b file:
CB<K>@<gs>). TSUM embeds the mandatory decomposition columns per image so
addendum 20.5's fail clause is auditable from the file alone; the
evaluator cross-checks TSUM against the raw T1 rows (rail, not trust).

## P-Q1-9 Verdicts live in the evaluator; failability proven

probe_sandbox.sh parses T1/TSUM rows, recomputes every derived figure,
prints the T1A VERDICT line (and T1B when its file exists) WITHOUT ever
flipping exit codes, and gains `--self-check-t1`: a fabricated consistent
frame must PASS, and named mutations (gate flip, retention breach, floor
breach, decomposition mismatch, sole-term lie) must each flip the readout.
Zero container bytes throughout; wall-clock logged beside the run per the
A3 precedent.
